mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW X3 xDrive28i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW X3 xDrive28i rebuilt engine typically costs £1,500-£3,000 supply-only for the N20B20A unit, with B48 units ranging £2,200-£4,000 and N52 units £1,800-£3,200. Used engines start from around £700, while reconditioned units sit in the middle at £1,200-£2,800. Supply and fit adds £1,000-£1,800 labour, bringing the total fitted cost to £2,500-£4,800 for a rebuilt unit.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW X3 xDrive28i N20 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs are a whining noise when the engine is revved and a rattling or clacking noise coming from the front of the engine on cold start. Other symptoms include loss of power, engine management light illumination, and in severe cases, engine failure. First signs typically appear from 60,000-100,000 miles. Pre-2015 N20 engines are at highest risk. Ignoring the rattle risks catastrophic engine damage - the chain can snap and destroy the engine.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW X3 xDrive28i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation. For F25 xDrive28i (2013-2017) examples valued £5,000-£14,000, a specialist-fitted rebuilt engine at £3,200-£4,500 may represent 40-60% of the vehicle's value - evaluate condition carefully. For G01 examples (2018-2024) valued £15,000+, replacement is comfortably within vehicle value. For N52-equipped early F25 examples (2010-2012), a rebuilt engine is often not cost-effective unless the car is in exceptional condition.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW X3 xDrive28i N52, N20 and B48 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The xDrive28i badge has been used across three different petrol engines. From 2010-2012, the N52B30 was a 3.0-litre naturally aspirated straight-six producing 260hp. From 2013-2017, the N20B20A was a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder producing 240hp. From 2018-2024, the B48B20A is a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder producing 245hp. The N20 and B48 are not interchangeable without significant modification - always match the engine code to your VIN.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW X3 xDrive28i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW X3 xDrive28i engine replacement takes 2-4 days for a specialist workshop, depending on the engine type and whether it's a like-for-like swap or a full rebuild. N20/N52 engine swap: 10-14 hours labour. B48 engine swap: 10-14 hours labour. Supply-only orders: 1-3 working days delivery. Allow additional time for diagnostic checks and road testing.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW X3 xDrive28i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW X3 xDrive28i badge represents a fascinating evolution in BMW's petrol engine strategy. From 2010 to 2012, the xDrive28i was powered by the naturally aspirated 3.0-litre N52 straight-six - BMW's last great naturally aspirated six-cylinder. But in a landmark shift for 2013, BMW replaced the six-cylinder with the 2.0-litre N20 TwinPower Turbo four-cylinder as part of its EfficientDynamics strategy. The turbo four delivered 240hp and 350Nm of torque - down 10kW in peak power but up 40Nm in torque compared to the outgoing six-cylinder. Later G01-generation models (2018-2024) adopted the B48B20A, a further evolution of BMW's modular petrol engine family.

milestones.description: 2012 - N52B30, 3.0-litre naturally aspirated straight-six, 260hp (F25 generation, early production)
2017 - N20B20A / N20B20B, 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder, 240hp (F25 generation, facelift)

commonProblems.h2: BMW X3 xDrive28i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW X3 xDrive28i has worn three different petrol engines across its production life - the naturally aspirated N52 straight-six (2010-2012), the turbocharged N20 four-cylinder (2013-2017), and the B48 four-cylinder (2018-2024). While the N52 is broadly reliable with age-related niggles, the N20 has a notorious Achilles heel: timing chain failure. Rebuilt BMW X3 xDrive28i engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded internal components designed to address the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N20 Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW X3 xDrive28i N20 Engine Fails Catastrophically
problems.rootCause: The N20's timing chain and plastic guides can develop slack, causing rapid wear on sprockets and guides. The chain tensioner is also prone to failure. If not addressed, the chain can snap, resulting in bent valves and catastrophic engine damage. BMW introduced a redesigned timing chain guide in January 2015.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets. Engine-out access on xDrive models.
repairOptions.longevity: Best caught early - whine or rattle on start-up. Adds 60k+ miles.

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - rebuilt N20 engine (supply & fit)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components, fitted, tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Chain has snapped or engine seized - only sensible option after catastrophic failure.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW X3 xDrive28i (F25, 2013-2017) is worth approximately £5,000-£14,000 depending on mileage, condition and trim `[INDUSTRY ESTIMATE]`. For N20-equipped F25 examples valued under £7,000, a full rebuilt engine may represent 40-60% of the vehicle's value - evaluate condition carefully before committing. G01 examples (2018-2024) with B48 engines are worth £15,000+ and replacement is comfortably within vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If your N20-powered xDrive28i makes a whining noise on revving or rattles on cold start, act immediately. The £1,500-£2,200 preventative chain replacement is far cheaper than a £3,200+ full rebuild. If you own a pre-2015 N20, treat the timing chain as a scheduled maintenance item at 80,000 miles.

problems.h4: N52 Water Pump & Oil Leaks - The Ageing Straight-Six's Weaknesses
problems.rootCause: The N52's electric water pump can fail without warning, leading to sudden overheating. Valve cover gaskets and oil filter housing gaskets commonly develop oil leaks as the engine ages.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electric water pump, thermostat, coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative replacement at 80k miles - avoids sudden failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gasket, spark plug tube seals
repairOptions.longevity: Fixes oil leaks before they damage other components

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - rebuilt N52 engine (supply & fit)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply rebuilt unit, fitted, tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Severe overheating has warped head - replacement is the only safe path

problems.recommendation: On the N52, the electric water pump is the biggest risk - it fails without warning and can destroy the engine through overheating. Replace it preventatively at 80,000 miles (£500-£800 at a specialist). Oil leaks are annoying but rarely catastrophic if caught early; address them when you see oil spots on your driveway.

problems.group: N20 & B48 Fuel Injector & HPFP Issues
problems.h4: N20 & B48 Fuel Injector & HPFP Issues - Petrol Turbo Weaknesses
problems.rootCause: Fuel injectors in the N20 and B48 engines can fail, leading to rough idling, poor fuel economy, and decreased performance. The high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) is also a known weak point.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnose failed injector, replace, code to ECU
repairOptions.longevity: Isolated failure on otherwise healthy engine

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all injectors, HPFP, fuel filter, oil change
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if one injector fails beyond 80k miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply rebuilt unit with new injectors and HPFP, fitted, tested
repairOptions.longevity: Injector failure has caused cylinder damage

problems.recommendation: If your xDrive28i is running rough or has poor fuel economy, have the injectors inspected. A single failed injector costs £250-£450 to replace at a specialist - cheap insurance against engine damage. On higher-mileage examples, replacing the full set preventatively at 80k miles is a sound investment.
